fieldValues.title: Protocol run execution over MCP
fieldValues.summary: srs-mcp gained six tools mirroring the CLI's srs protocol run verbs (create/advance/get/list/complete/abandon), closing the deferral recorded when #965 shipped only the read-only Protocol definition resources.
fieldValues.body:
## What changed

`crates/srs-mcp/src/tools.rs` gained `protocol_run_create`, `protocol_run_advance`, `protocol_run_get`, `protocol_run_list`, `protocol_run_complete`, `protocol_run_abandon` — shadow input structs mirroring `protocol_run_service`'s typed inputs field-for-field, each handler exactly one service call (ADR-037). No changes to `srs-repository` or the CLI: this is a pure adapter over the six functions the CLI's `srs protocol run ...` verbs already call.

## Why this unit could proceed as Door 1

#965's own PR body classified the read-only Protocol resources as Door 1 (capability-layering adapter) and named the run verbs as an explicit, conditional follow-up ("if run state should be agent-visible"). #977 supplied that condition: the programme's own `programme-unit-walk` Protocol (srs#580) is the first consumer that needs an agent to observe and advance run state without shelling out to the CLI. No new normative meaning was introduced — same classification as #965.

## Proof

`cargo build/test/clippy --workspace` all exit 0 with `SRS_SPEC_DIR` pointed at a fresh `origin/master` clone of `srs` (srs-rust#874's mechanism). New integration tests cover the full run lifecycle (create -> advance -> complete, create -> abandon) including the state-machine guard rejecting a second complete/abandon/advance on a non-Active run, plus list filtering by status and protocolId. The malformed-request guard (missing required `stageId`) was proven red on purpose - temporarily loosened the shadow struct's field to `Option`, watched the integration test fail exactly there, then reverted - before this PR shipped.

PR: the-greenman/srs-rust#983.
